title: 1 Samuel 18
paragraphs: ¹ By the time David had finished speaking with Saul, Jonathan felt a deep bond with David and loved him as he loved himself. ² From that day on, Saul kept David with him and wouldn't let him return to his father's house. ³ Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself. ⁴ Jonathan took off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt. ⁵ David went out on every mission Saul sent him on and was so successful that Saul gave him a high rank in the army. This pleased all the people and Saul's officers as well.

⁶ When the men were returning home after David killed the Philistine, women came out from all the towns of Israel to meet King Saul with singing and dancing, with joyful songs and tambourines and lyres. ⁷ As they danced, the women sang: "Saul has killed his thousands, and David his tens of thousands." ⁸ Saul was furious, and the song displeased him. He said, "They have credited David with tens of thousands, but me with only thousands. What more can he have but the kingdom?" ⁹ And from that time on, Saul kept a jealous eye on David. ¹⁰ The next day an evil spirit from God came powerfully upon Saul. He was raving inside his house while David was playing the lyre, as he did each day. Saul had a spear in his hand,

¹¹ and Saul hurled the spear, thinking, "I'll pin David to the wall." But David dodged him twice. ¹² Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul. ¹³ So Saul sent David away from him and gave him command of a thousand men. David led the troops in their campaigns. ¹⁴ In everything he did he was very successful, because the LORD was with him. ¹⁵ When Saul saw how successful David was, he was afraid of him. ¹⁶ But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them in their campaigns.

¹⁶ All Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them in battle and was always out in front with them. ¹⁷ Saul said to David, "Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you in marriage; in return, serve me bravely and fight the LORD's battles." Saul thought, "I won't raise my hand against him. Let the Philistines do that." ¹⁸ But David said to Saul, "Who am I, and what is my family or my father's clan in Israel, that I should become the king's son-in-law?" ¹⁹ But when the time came for Merab to be given to David, she was instead given to Adriel of Meholah to be his wife. ²⁰ Meanwhile, Michal, Saul's other daughter, had fallen in love with David, and when Saul was told about it, he was pleased.

²¹ Saul thought, "I'll give her to him so that she can be a trap for him and the Philistines can strike him down." So Saul said to David, "You have a second chance to become my son-in-law." ²² Then Saul instructed his servants, "Talk to David privately and say to him, 'The king is pleased with you, and his attendants all like you. Become his son-in-law.'" ²³ So Saul's servants said these things to David. But David replied, "Do you think it's easy to become the king's son-in-law? I'm just a poor man with no reputation." ²⁴ When his servants reported back to Saul what David had said, ²⁵ Saul replied, "Say to David, 'The king wants no other payment for the bride than a hundred Philistine foreskins, to take revenge on his enemies.'" Saul's plan was to have David fall at the hands of the Philistines.

²⁶ When his servants told this to David, David was pleased at the prospect of becoming the king's son-in-law. Before the deadline arrived, ²⁷ David and his men went and killed two hundred Philistines. David brought back their foreskins and presented the full number to the king so that he could become the king's son-in-law. Then Saul gave him his daughter Michal in marriage. ²⁸ When Saul realized that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved David, ²⁹ Saul became even more afraid of him, and he remained his enemy for the rest of his life. ³⁰ The Philistine commanders kept coming out to fight, but whenever they did, David was more successful than all the rest of Saul's officers, and his fame spread widely.
